messages:
mike_support: Heads-up — NovaView (customer) completed the OIDC flow but their console shows NO API key. They report 403 on all calls. Can ops check provisioning? :eyes:

alex_ops: Can you paste the project/org identifiers from the onboarding email and a sample failing request?

mike_support: Project slug from email: novaview-prod-2026, org id: org_98765. Sample failing curl from customer:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":{"code":403,"message":"API key not authorized for any project"}}
```

sam_eng: Quick check: list-keys for their org shows a key but it's tied to project "ghost-staging-123" (internal). CLI output I pulled from admin DB query:
```
> SELECT api_key, project_slug, org_id FROM api_keys WHERE org_id='org_98765';
api_7f9a, ghost-staging-123, org_98765
```

mike_support: Wait — that shows a key exists but in the wrong project. Customer expects novaview-prod-2026. How would a key for their org be bound to ghost-staging-123?

provision-bot: Provisioner job #p-3321 created service account 'svc-provisioner-394' and claimed tenant=novaview-prod-2026. Binding job attempted: bind_claim->project_slug_normalized='ghost-staging-123' (matched existing project id).

jess_sre: This smells like a slug normalization collision — two slugs normalized to same canonical id. Check the normalization rules and whether trailing tokens were dropped. Also need an audit entry so we can notify the customer and rotate keys if we rebind.

sam_eng: Repro steps I ran locally: create claim tenant='NovaView-Prod-2026' -> normalization lowercases + strip non-alphanum -> 'novaviewprod2026'. We recently added logic to truncate to 15 chars for legacy compat; 'novaviewprod2026' -> 'novaviewprod20' which collides with 'ghost-staging-123' canonicalized earlier due to similar prefix. Bug.

alex_ops: Ops action plan: 1) Rebind the API key to novaview-prod-2026 project manually (non-destructive) so customer traffic is restored. 2) Create new API key scoped to the correct project and mark old key as revoked after migration. 3) Run one-off backfill to detect other potential collisions. 4) Postmortem and permanent fix for slug normalization.

mike_support: Can someone run the rebind and create a temporary key for them? Customer is blocked in prod. I can message NovaView that we're on it.

alex_ops: I'll run the manual rebind now (will log the request). Command I'm using (admin only):
```
adminctl rebind-key --org org_98765 --from-project ghost-staging-123 --to-project novaview-prod-2026 --key api_7f9a --audit "manual rebind for customer outage"
```

provision-bot: Action logged: rebind-request id=r-7742 by alex_ops at 2026-03-17T15:12:30Z.

alex_ops: Done. I've re-bound api_7f9a to novaview-prod-2026 and generated a new key api_8b2c for them as well. Rotated and added note in audit.

mike_support: :tada: Passing new key to customer via secure channel now. Will confirm they can call.

nova_admin: Confirmed — new key works, calls now return 200. Thanks for fast response.

jess_sre: Please open a bug with high priority for the slug-truncation normalization and schedule a short runbook for manual rebinds. Also include a query to detect existing collisions.

sam_eng: Filed PROD-1298 with repro, root cause and mitigation steps. Will follow up with a patch to normalization logic and unit tests.

mike_support: Closing the ticket once customer verifies in 24h. Thanks everyone. :pray:
